basics.name: Juyi Lin
basics.label: PhD Student in Computer Engineering
basics.summary: PhD student at Northeastern University working on generative world models, video reasoning benchmarks, and efficient Vision-Language-Action models. Advisor: Prof. Yanzhi Wang.

education.institution: King Abdullah University of Science and Technology

work.name: Futurewei Technologies, Inc.
work.summary: Research Intern, Generative AI & World Modeling team.
highlights: Built LEAP end to end on Qwen3-Omni-30B-A3B for hour-scale audio-visual QA: the localization and answer stages, their two LoRAs, and the evaluation harness behind all reported numbers.
Method: per-block localization picks evidence windows; one bounded answer pass re-encodes only those windows.

Results: +4.5–16.8 pp over the Qwen3-Omni baseline on TraceAV, LVOmni, VideoOdyssey (1–4 h) and MMOU; transfers to MiniCPM-o 4.5 (+3.1–13.0 pp over its published results); answer input and peak context stay independent of recording duration; supports causal/streaming queries without streaming-specific training.

work.name: Beijing VirtAI Tech
highlights: Integrated the PaddlePaddle distributed training library and Deep Graph Library (DGL) into the in-house performance measurement system, extending it to two new framework backends.
Profiled PaddlePaddle distributed training and reported its scaling bottlenecks to the platform team.

projects.name: Physical Reasoning Benchmark for Generative World Models
highlights: Proposed and built PhyGround, a criteria-grounded benchmark for physical reasoning in generative video world models built on 250 curated prompts and a taxonomy of 13 physical laws (mechanics, fluids, optics); evaluated 8 video models against it.
Led a large-scale human annotation study: 459 annotators, 5,796 complete annotations, 37.4K+ fine-grained labels, with split-half ranking correlation Spearman's ρ > 0.90.
Trained and released PhyJudge-9B, an open physics-specialized VLM judge reaching 3.3% aggregate relative bias vs. 16.6% for Gemini-3.1-Pro.

projects.name: Video Reasoning Benchmark
highlights: Proposed and co-led (team of 22) VBVR-EvalKit, a reasoning benchmark for video generation models, evaluating 9 models (4 proprietary, 5 open-weight).
Designed the data-generation and benchmark framework, set the roadmap, and contributed core code and evaluation metrics; shipped an open-source ecosystem with 100+ synthetic data generators.
Built a dataset of 200 curated reasoning tasks and 1M+ video clips, 1000× larger than prior datasets; released eval suite = 100 tasks × 5 samples (500 videos).

projects.name: Vision Language Action (VLA) Model
projects.summary: NEU & Funded by EmbodyX, Jan 2025 – Sept 2025
highlights: Proposed VOTE, a fine-tuning framework for parallel VLA action prediction, using an ensemble voting strategy over sampled actions to cut compute while improving success and generalization; adopted by Cisco and EmbodyX.
+20% average success over OpenVLA across four LIBERO suites, +7% over the state-of-the-art VLA model on SimplerEnv WidowX, and 39× faster action generation on NVIDIA Jetson Orin.
Pretrained Llama3.2-1B into a VLM and fine-tuned it with VOTE, beating 7B OpenVLA by 16% average success across the four LIBERO suites.
